added_failures_note: the reviewed run is an evidence node whose write paths reach no test file and whose manifest declares no baseline_suite or after_suite, so there is no base or head suite log and no failure ids to derive; the run's own gates (verify/falsify/overlap/guard/quiet/negcontrol/readback) each reported EXIT=0, and I independently reproduced verify to EXIT=0 with all five checks true.

assertion_analysis.condition_to_fail: A supersede fails to lower the live unchained_holder count, so it stays above before-minus-targets; falsify.log:2 shows exactly this check reddening when the baseline count is incremented.
The unchained-holder set is not exactly the stored baseline minus the retired targets, e.g. a name enters the population; the live set and the stored baseline are independent sides.
A retired target carries no StandardNameChange with the authority's file digest, so targets minus receipt_targets is non-empty.
A target survives with a name_stage/status pair other than superseded/superseded.

A foreign change, source write or name update lands inside the apply window; the window is positive-controlled by the 11 own receipts in changes_in_window. The settled_name_updates disjunct cannot fire for supersede-class writes (see finding) so it contributes no signal either way.
The planted different-quantity pair is admitted by the floors, so negcontrol mode exits non-zero; negative_control.refused is true at head.

findings.text: follow-on: the overlap read's name-update disjunct (StandardName.updated_at within the window) is empty for this node's own supersede writes — a direct read of the 11 retired targets shows their updated_at is from September 2026 (9/7-9/10), not the 02:29:38Z apply — so that component of the `overlap` boolean cannot fire for supersede-class writers; the read stands on foreign_changes (positive-controlled by the 11 own receipts) and foreign_sources, but the empty column must not be read as an independent clean check.

follow-on: the apply path (mode apply -> _signed_call(True, digest)) never calls quiet_graph_check, so the brief's guard 'apply only on a quiet graph' remains a procedure the operator must remember; a replayed apply would proceed on a busy graph, and the corrected owner probe is not bound to the write it is meant to protect. The pre-apply quiet probe was vacuous at apply time and is only replaced retrospectively by the overlap read.
